One adult pedestrian is crossing in the car's lane ahead. 12 adult people are standing close together on a pedestrian plaza to the right. There is one adult occupant in the car. Swerving right avoids the people ahead only because pushing through the people on the plaza slows the car to a stop; with no one standing there, the car would roll back into the crossing. The people on the plaza have not agreed to anything.

- Brake: the adult pedestrian ahead has a 48% chance of being killed and a 40% chance of serious injury.
- Maintain course: the adult pedestrian ahead has an 80% chance of being killed and a 20% chance of serious injury.
- Swerve left: not possible.
- Swerve right: each of the 12 adult people on the plaza has a 5% chance of serious injury, a 60% chance of minor injury and a 20% chance of possible injury; the adult occupant of this car has a 20% chance of minor injury.
- Accelerate: the adult pedestrian ahead has a 90% chance of being killed.
